svg.title: See the constraint behind the handoff
svg.desc: A hypothetical equipment-delivery team examines why apparently workable schedules create delays. Sam, a route planner, joins courier Jo on deliveries and sees missing entry instructions trigger calls, waiting, and extra handover work. Jo joins booking and planning and sees that narrow time windows are promised before access requirements are established. They check these interpretations together and change their shared handoff: capture access details before confirming a narrow window, allow for entry and handover in planning, and try the changes on selected routes. Follow-up checks both avoidable waiting and whether booking staff can use the process. Reciprocal visits are illustrative and need not have equal duration. Observation is for learning and does not establish competence to perform the other role.

g.text: See the constraint behind the handoff
Hypothetical delivery team · Experience the work, check the interpretation, change the arrangement
Where do our delivery plans create preventable waiting?
Driving time is only part of the job.
Capture access details before confirming a narrow delivery window.
Include entry and handover in planning.
Try on selected routes; check the effect at both ends.
Check for less avoidable waiting and a workable booking process.
Fictional observations and changes · Visits need not be reciprocal or equal in duration.
Observation develops understanding; independent performance requires appropriate preparation.
